Done. opaque type Lag in Seconds.scala, with Lag.between(onset, at) as the single boundary conversion, plus ofSeconds / rewound / advanced / isCausal and an Ordering. Hrf.apply, .at, .eval, .evalScalar, evaluateInSupport, ScalarHrf.scalarAt, Hrf.of/scalar/multi lambdas, every HrfFunctions shape fn, Evaluate, Deriv, Decorators, LwuBasis, Toeplitz, PulseResponse and Regressor all speak Lag.

Deviation from the proposal, deliberate: Seconds - Seconds still yields Seconds. Seconds also names widths and horizons (span, duration, precision), so an algebra where a - b is a Lag but a + b is a width is incoherent, and changing it would have rippled outside the module — contradicting the small blast radius this bead is premised on. The safety comes instead from Lag.between being the only way in, called in exactly one place (Regressor.evalLoop).

Blast radius was as predicted: one external call site, design/.../HrfGeneratorsSuite.scala:26.

New LagSuite pins the type-level claim with scala.compiletime.testing.typeChecks: Hrfs.SPMG1(onset: Seconds) does not compile, and neither does Hrfs.boxcar(width = someLag).

Verified JVM+JS: hrf 178, hrf-laws 77, design 146 at that point.
